facts.raw_span: persistent swelling of his left breast for four years
ultrasonography had shown gynecomastia (BIRADS II) attributed to anabolic-steroid use
a new, mildly tender, firm 1-cm subareolar mass under the left nipple
Repeat ultrasonography demonstrates a 1.5-cm long, solid structure with lobular architecture
Mammography reveals a lobulated retroareolar mass approximately 1.5 cm in diameter without microcalcifications (BIRADS III)
anabolic-steroid use, which he discontinued

concepts.why: The patient has a history of anabolic-steroid use, which is a known cause of gynecomastia, and initial ultrasonography showed gynecomastia.

The patient presents with a new, mildly tender, firm mass under the left nipple, and repeat ultrasonography demonstrates a solid structure with lobular architecture, which is consistent with fibroadenoma.

The patient presents with a new, mildly tender mass under the left nipple, and repeat ultrasonography demonstrates a solid structure, but a breast cyst is also a possible diagnosis given the clinical presentation.

The patient presents with a new, mildly tender, firm mass under the left nipple, and repeat ultrasonography demonstrates a solid structure with lobular architecture, which is consistent with phyllodes tumor.
The patient has a history of persistent swelling of his left breast, and anabolic-steroid use, which can cause pseudogynecomastia.
The patient presents with a new, mildly tender mass under the left nipple, which could be consistent with a subareolar abscess.

rationales.F01: Persistent swelling is more typical of gynecomastia or pseudogynecomastia.
rationales.F02: Previous ultrasonography showing gynecomastia attributed to anabolic-steroid use strongly supports gynecomastia.
rationales.F03: A new, mildly tender, firm mass could be a fibroadenoma, breast cyst, phyllodes tumor, or subareolar abscess.
rationales.F04: Solid structure with lobular architecture on ultrasonography could indicate fibroadenoma or phyllodes tumor.
rationales.F05: Lobulated retroareolar mass on mammography without microcalcifications could indicate fibroadenoma or phyllodes tumor.
rationales.F06: Discontinued anabolic-steroid use may reduce the likelihood of gynecomastia but could still be present.

frontier_selector.rationale: The new, mildly tender, firm 1-cm subareolar mass and the ultrasonography and mammography findings of a solid structure with lobular architecture and a lobulated retroareolar mass support Fibroadenoma, which is a more specific diagnosis than Gynecomastia.
